conventions.unverified: The literal string 'unverified' (and the top-level 'unverified' list) means no fetched source stated the value. Nothing was guessed, averaged, interpolated or filled from memory.
conventions.src: Every fact carries 'src', a list of ids in the top-level 'sources' array (U1...). Child objects without their own src inherit the nearest parent's.
conventions.quotes: 'quote' (and 'quote_samples', 'qualifier_quote', 'how_to_read_quote') strings are verbatim from the saved source text (pdftotext -layout or raw, HTML-to-text, or source code). Line breaks and table-cell wraps were joined; pdftotext glyph artifacts (e.g. '11⁄2' for 1 1/2, '2⅕') are kept. HTML sub/superscripts come out as spaced inline text ('ft 2', 'Ra 1/4').
conventions.quote_check: The merge script searched every quote not flagged from_image in the saved text of its cited source(s) (NFKC, whitespace-collapsed; then whitespace-insensitive; then in-order word fragments for interleaved PDF table cells). 'quote_check' records the result. All checked quotes were found.
conventions.from_image: Quotes and values flagged from_image were read from an equation image, a rendered PDF page or a chart. Chart values marked digitized / agent_digitized are pixel readings with the stated uncertainty, NOT printed numbers.
conventions.agent_checks: methods_notes.agent_consistency_checks are computed by the research agent from sourced formulas or printed values. They are cross-checks only, not source values.
conventions.distributor_copies: Sources flagged distributor_copy are manufacturer PDFs hosted by distributors (Zoro, Baker, Gemaire, Watsco, allnoisecontrol); prefer the official sheet where both exist.

flat_surface_heat_transfer.summary: ASTM C680-style outer-surface coefficient for a flat duct face = h_conv (natural/forced blend) + h_rad, with air properties at the film temperature (same property formulas and radiation term as the pipe engine; see calc-method-verified.json surface_heat_transfer). Orientation sets the natural-convection correlation and the blend exponent j (D = 0 for all flat surfaces). For a horizontal rectangular duct: the two sides are vertical flat surfaces (L = side height); the top and bottom are horizontal flat surfaces (L = A/P). For HOT faces the top uses the 'unstable' correlation (0.54/0.15) and the bottom the 'stable' one (0.27); for COLD faces (cooling ducts) ASHRAE, Lienhard and the C680-89 shape factors swap them: the BOTTOM of a cold duct is the unstable face and the TOP is the stable face.

Figure 8. R-Value Required to Prevent Condensation on Surface with Emittance ε = 0.9

Preventing surface condensation requires that sufficient thermal resistance be installed for the condensation design conditions. Figures 7 and 8 give installed R-value requirements to prevent surface condensation on insulated air ducts. The first chart (for emittance = 0.1) should be used for foil-faced insulation products. The second chart is based on materials with a surface emittance of 0.9.

Rather, the worst case for condensation occurs when relative humidity is high, such as when the dry bulb is only very slightly above the wet bulb. This condition often occurs in the early morning in many climates.

cross_checks.topic: ASHRAE F23 Figs. 7/8 vs NAIMA AH139 Fig. 1 (two independent digitizations)
cross_checks.summary: NAIMA AH139 Fig. 1 / AH121 Figs. 20-21 plot required installed R vs ambient 60-100 F for 60/70/80/90% RH, emissivity 0.1 (FSK) and 0.9 (vinyl, PSK), and state '55 F cold duct internal temperature and no air movement on the external surface'. ASHRAE F23 Figs. 7/8 plot the same four RH curves at the same two emittances but print no duct temperature or wind. Comparing the main agent's ASHRAE digitization with the install sub-agent's NAIMA digitization at 70/80/90/100 F: eps 0.9 panel 90% RH 4.36/7.89/9.84/11.35 (ASHRAE) vs 4.4/8.0/10.1/11.7 (NAIMA); 80% RH 1.11/2.38/3.39/4.13 vs 1.2/2.7/3.7/4.4; eps 0.1 panel 80% RH 2.97/6.04/9.11/10.65 vs 3.1/6.5/9.2/11.4; 70% RH 1.82/2.78/4.12/5.37 vs 1.5/2.9/4.2/5.6. Agreement is within the combined reading error (about 0.2-0.7 R), so the ASHRAE charts are very likely the NAIMA curves re-drawn (ASHRAE extends the eps 0.1, 90% RH curve to R 37.7 at 100 F where NAIMA's axis stops at R 12). This is an agent comparison; ASHRAE itself does not state 55 F or still air.

agent_consistency_checks.topic: Rayleigh numbers on duct faces (agent arithmetic)
agent_consistency_checks.summary: With the C680 air properties at a 65 F film temperature, a 2 ft tall duct side at |dT| = 20 F has Ra_L = 2.7e8 (below the 1e9 switch, so C680's laminar vertical form applies); a 24 in wide duct top or bottom with L_ch ~ W/2 = 1 ft has Ra = 3.4e7 at |dT| = 20 F and 8.5e6 at 5 F, i.e. above ASHRAE's 8e6 switch (0.15 Ra^1/3) but below the DNV-printed 1e8 switch (0.54 Ra^1/4). The 1e8 vs 8e6 conflict (flat_surface_heat_transfer.horizontal_flat.unstable_face.conflict) therefore matters for ducts.

agent_consistency_checks.topic: Which face of a cold duct runs coldest (agent inference)
agent_consistency_checks.summary: For a cold duct the stable faces are the TOP (heat flowing down into it) and the unstable face is the BOTTOM. The stable correlation (0.27 Ra^1/4) gives the lowest convective coefficient, so for equal insulation the top surface sits closest to the duct temperature and reaches dew point first; ASHRAE Ch. 26 Table 10 shows the same ordering for still air (heat flow downward R 0.92 vs upward 0.61 at eps 0.9). No fetched source states 'condensation starts on the top of a duct'.

agent_consistency_checks.topic: Inside-film magnitude for typical duct air (agent arithmetic, for orientation only)
agent_consistency_checks.summary: ASHRAE T8.17a at t = 55 F, V = 1000 fpm (16.7 ft/s), D_h = 1.5 ft gives h_i = (0.3323 - 0.0131) x 16.7^0.8 / 1.5^0.2 = about 2.8 Btu/h ft2 F (R_i about 0.36); the MIDG duct calculator's lumped 0.85 (inside + outside) is consistent with R_i about 0.2-0.4 plus a still-air outside film of about 0.5-0.7. Inside film matters for bare or thinly insulated ducts and is small against R-6 to R-12 wraps.

ASHRAE Ch. 23 Eq. (3) is the linear (single-pass, fixed q) form; the MIDG/ASHRAE Ch. 4 Eq. (39) exponential form is the exact solution for constant U. For the ASHRAE Example 1 numbers (dT 4.9 F on an 82 F difference) the two differ by under 0.2 F (agent arithmetic). The 0.2 factor = 144 in2/ft2 / (60 min/h x 12 in/ft) (agent reading of 'conversion factor for length, time units').

agent_consistency_checks.topic: Installed R = installed thickness / installed k (agent arithmetic on printed values)
agent_consistency_checks.summary: OC SOFTR FRK Type 75, 2 in. nominal: installed thickness 1.5 in / installed k 0.27 = R 5.56, printed installed R 5.6; out-of-package 2 in / 0.30 = 6.67, printed 6.8 (printed values are rounded from the manufacturer's own k, so a 0.1-0.2 R mismatch on out-of-package values is expected).
